name: Justin Jefferson

background.fact: Justin Jamal Jefferson was born June 16, 1999, and attended Destrehan High School in Destrehan, Louisiana. He was a low three-star prospect (247Sports ranked him 308th among wide receivers) and committed to LSU.
He played three years at LSU under head coach Ed Orgeron and won the 2020 College Football Playoff National Championship as a junior.

Minnesota drafted him in the first round (22nd overall) of the 2020 NFL draft. He has been named to the Pro Bowl and All-Pro team in four of his first five seasons and has the most receiving yards through a player's first five seasons in NFL history.

background.fact: In 2022, at age 23, he became the youngest player to lead the league in receptions (128) and receiving yards (1,809) and won NFL Offensive Player of the Year.
Listed at 6 ft 1 in, 195 lb, age 27, jersey 18, in his seventh NFL season. Combine: 4.43 forty, 37.5 inch vertical, 126 inch broad jump.
He signed a four-year extension worth $140 million with $110 million guaranteed, reported as the richest deal for a non-quarterback at the time. The deal dates from 2024, not 2026.

scouts_read: Jefferson is healthy and not on the injury report, so he should play most of the snaps. The bigger question is the quarterback: Cousins arrived on Tuesday, and the pair was productive together from 2020 to 2023 while Jefferson has been at a career-low pace this season. With Hockenson out and Addison questionable, Jefferson should see heavy targets, likely 9 to 12. The line suggests a low scoring game with Minnesota near 20 points, and Green Bay is described as good against deep throws, which caps the touchdown upside. I would project a solid 11 to 15 point game with a ceiling near 25 if he gets a touchdown, as he did in the Week 1 meeting.
